pipelines-flush-backpressure.title: Treat PipeWriter.FlushAsync as a backpressure boundary
pipelines-flush-backpressure.short: A flush can asynchronously wait for the reader
pipelines-flush-backpressure.summary: System.IO.Pipelines coordinates producers and consumers; FlushAsync is where a writer can observe completion, cancellation, and pressure from buffered data.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.why: Ignoring the asynchronous flush boundary can let a producer outrun its consumer or mishandle shutdown.
pipelines-flush-backpressure.tips: Await flushes, inspect completion when appropriate, and keep ownership of the writer clear through shutdown.

socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.title: Understand dual-mode sockets when supporting IPv4 and IPv6
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.short: One IPv6 socket can accept mapped IPv4 endpoints when configured
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.summary: A dual-mode IPv6 socket can reduce duplicated listener logic while still serving IPv4 clients on supported platforms.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.why: Assuming address-family behavior is identical everywhere can cause listeners or endpoint comparisons to fail unexpectedly.
socket-dualmode-ipv6-ipv4.tips: Choose dual-mode behavior deliberately, test deployment platforms, and normalize endpoint handling where address representation matters.

dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.title: Use alternate dictionary lookup to avoid temporary key allocations
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.short: Query compatible key representations without materializing a new key
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.summary: Alternate lookup APIs can let compatible key representations such as spans participate in dictionary lookup without first allocating a temporary object.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.why: Creating a short-lived string for every lookup can dominate allocation in parsing-heavy hot paths.
dictionary-alternate-lookup-span-key.tips: Use only when the comparer supports the alternate representation and measurement shows temporary key creation matters.

xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.title: Stream large XML and configure XmlReader for untrusted input
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.short: Avoid unnecessary full-document materialization and unsafe resolver behavior
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.summary: XmlReader provides forward-only XML processing and explicit settings for DTD and external resource handling.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.why: Blindly loading large or untrusted XML can create avoidable memory pressure and unsafe external-resource behavior.
xmlreader-streaming-untrusted-input.tips: Disable features you do not need, impose application-level size limits, and process large documents incrementally.

assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.title: Resolve managed and native plugin assets with AssemblyDependencyResolver
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.short: Plugin dependency resolution should follow the plugin's dependency context
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.summary: AssemblyDependencyResolver maps assembly and unmanaged-library names to assets associated with a plugin component.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.why: Searching arbitrary directories manually can select incompatible versions and breaks native dependency resolution easily.
assemblydependencyresolver-plugin-native.tips: Pair the resolver with a dedicated AssemblyLoadContext and keep plugin loading policy explicit.
